text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Temp agency Start signs deal with insurer Nationale Nederlanden to offer temping services through network of independent brokers. (p1)
- Services sector profits grow fastest, according to Central Bureau of Statistics (CBS). (p1)
- Material handling systems maker VanderLande Industries taken over by Japan's Daifuku. (p1)
- Amsterdam AEX-index breaks through 600 point barrier despite options exchange market makers' attempts to keep it under 600. (p1)
- Social affairs minister Ad Melkert recommends Dutch social-economic policy at OECD conference, "Beyond 2000: The New Social Policy Agenda". (p1)
- Profit growth of insurer Delta Llyod slows. (p3)
- Cable maker Draka takes over cable activities of French participation company GIFI. (p3)
- The number of new businesses set up in the Netherlands rose 60 pct between 1987 and 1994, says report by economic institute EIM.
-VOLKSKRANT
- Fruit and vegetables auctions merger The Greenery to shed 1,500 jobs, says union FNV. (p1)
- Surinam aluminium production, which stopped on Tuesday, will probably never start again due to lack of funds. (p1)
- Share prices on Amsterdam Stock Exchange forced up by investors' fear of missing out on profits. (p2)
- Bank insurer ING breathes new life into savings bank NMS. (p33)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Most Dutch have lost trust in Public Prosectur's office - research. (p1)
- PTT Telecom cannot handle large demand for ISDN connections. (p33)
- Three options traders arrested on alleged insider trading in BolsWessanen. (p33)
- 131 Dutch bourse-listed companies book two pct higher net in 1996 H1. (p35)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Unrest grows among staff of container transhipment group ECT about Danish container group Maersk's plans for own terminal. (p9)
- Junior finance minister to press European Union at next meeting for measures against tax evasion on Internet. (p9)
TROUW
- Coalition parties clash over sending troops to Zaire. (p4) -
